BEFORE:
HON'BLE JUSTICE RAJASEKHAR MANTHA HON'BLE JUSTICE SUPRATIM
BHATTACHARYA
DATE: 13TH JULY 2023.

APPEARANC  Mr. Sakya Sen, Adv.; Mr. A. Banerjee, Adv.; Mr. S. Ghosh, Adv.; Mr. R. Mullick, Adv  S.Maity, Adv., for peti  Mr. K. Chatterjee, Adv.; Mr. M. L. Banerjee, Adv.; Mr. S. Mal, Adv., for responden RAJASEKHAR MANTHA, J.:
1.
THE COURT:

IA No.GA/8/2023 has been filed seeking recall of the order dated July 11, 2023,
passed by this Court.
The order is set out hereinbelow:

"THE COURT: The Registrar, Original Side, of this Court has placed a note referring to a letter of Mr. Mohanlal Banerjee, learned Advocate, representing the Life Insurance Corporation of India, seeking return of Rs.92 lakhs, lying with the Registrar, original Side, and kept in deposit in aid of APO/288/2016.
Heatly Gresham (India) Pvt Ltd & Anr vs Life Insurance Corporation Of India

By an order dated December 20, 2019, a Division Bench of this Court directed that the appellants may seek appropriate orders in respect of the said sum of Rs.92 lakhs,
lying with the Registrar, Original Side, within a period of eight weeks from the said date.
It was further ordered that if no formal decision of any Court was obtained by the appellants, LICI would be entitled to the release of the said sum of money in their favour on first demand.
The appellants were also given liberty to file a suit if they were of the view that the LICI was not entitled to the entire sum of Rs.92 lakhs.
Admittedly, no such suit has been filed.
There is an application pending under Article 227 being CO/112/2020 filed by the appellants, in which no order has been passed in favour of the appellants.
Counsel for the LICI submits that the appellants have already vacated the said premises and the same is in the custody of the LICI.
In the above circumstances, this Court directs the Registrar, Original side of this Court to release the entire sum of Rs.92 lakhs together with any accrued interest to the LICI by way of a cheque.
The cheque may be received by an authorised officer of the LICI upon production of the letter of authority in terms of this order.
Let the LICI collect the aforesaid payment within a period of 7 days from date.

The reference by the Registrar, Original Side of this Court, is accordingly disposed of."
2.

It is argued by Mr. Sakya Sen, learned counsel for the applicants, that the Court had become functus officio and hence by reason of the order dated December 20, 2009, passed in APO/288/2016, by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court,
the question of this Court entertaining any clarification from the Registrar, Original Side of this Court did not and could not arise.

3. He further submits that the learned Advocate who represented his clients on July 11, 2023,
appeared after finding the matter in the cause list and apprised this Court that the appeal stood disposed of and had appeared by mistake.
4. It is argued that no formal notice was received by the applicants of the matter being listed before this court either at the instance of the Registrar, Original Side, or the LICI.
5. Mr. Sen relies upon two decisions of the Supreme Court to support his arguments that once an appeal is disposed of, no further order can be passed by the said Court as it becomes functus officio.
The said decisions are- (a) State of U.P. vs. Brahm Datt Sharma & anr., reported in AIR 1987 SC 943 (paragraph 10 thereof);

2 (b) Dy. Director, Land Acquisition -vs- Malla Atchinaidu & ors., reported in (2006) 12 SCC 87 (paragraph 48).

6. The matter was mentioned on behalf of the applicants on July 11, 2023 after the order was passed,
indicating that a revisional application was pending before a Single Bench of this Court being CO/112/2020.
It was also orally indicated to the court that there are restraint orders passed in the said revisional application.

7. It appears from the submissions of Mr. Sen today that except an order restraining the LICI from creating third party interest in the premises obtained back by them under orders of the Estate Officer, there are no other orders passed by the revisional Court.

The aforesaid fact is relevant since in the order dated December 20, 2019, disposing of APO/288/2016, at the operative part, a co-ordinate Bench had directed as follows:
"The appellants say that a sum of Rs.92 lakh has been deposited pursuant to orders passed in this appeal.

So that the appellants are not prejudiced, particularly since the orders were passed by this court, the deposits would be held by the Registrar,
Original Side for a period of eight weeks from today.
During such time, it will be open to the appellants herein to pursue their remedies in accordance with law in respect of the appellate order passed under the said Act of 1971.
It will also be open to the appellants herein to seek appropriate directions as regards the deposit that has been made pursuant to the previous orders passed in this appeal.
The deposit will abide by the decision of the appropriate forum.

However, if no decision of the appropriate forum is forthcoming within the period indicated hereinabove, the Registrar, Original Side must release the money to the Life Insurance Corporate of India upon its first written demand.

Even in such a situation, if the appellants herein perceive that the payment to LIC is beyond what LIC is entitled to in law, it will be open to the appellants to institute a suit for recovery of such amount or part of it as the appellants may be entitled in accordance with law."
8.

It is clear and apparent from the submissions of Mr. Sen and the documents annexed to IA No.GA/8/2023 that there is no restraint order on the LICI from obtaining return of the sums of money deposited with the Registrar, Original Side from any court or forum.

The Registrar, Original Side was receiving repeated letters from the LICI in terms of the rights conferred on them by the co-ordinate Bench in the order dated December 20, 2019 (supra), as set out hereinabove.
The Registrar, Original Side was only seeking a clarification from this Court.
9. In view of the facts narrated above, this Court is unable to accept the submissions of Mr. Sen that this Court had no jurisdiction to pass the order dated July 11, 2023.
The Registrar, Original Side was only seeking specific directions to carry out the order dated December 20, 2019, passed by the co-ordinate Bench (supra).

10. Insofar as the decisions cited before this Court by Mr. Sen, it is seen as follows:
Heatly Gresham (India) Pvt Ltd & Anr vs Life Insurance Corporation Of India ... on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47441871/

sentences.text: (a) In the case of State of U.P. vs. Brahm Datt Sharma & anr. (supra), the Supreme Court was dealing with an application filed in a disposed of writ petition passed on subsequent events.

entities.text: State of U.P. vs. Brahm Datt Sharma & anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was found by the Supreme Court that the subsequent events could at best give a separate cause of action to the applicants and hence the High Court was not justified in entertaining the application filed by the parties concerned in the disposed of writ petition.
It is in that context that the Supreme Court observed that the High Court had then, in that matter, become "functus officio".
(b) In the instant case, it is seen that there were certain contingent actions and entitlements that were stipulated in the order dated December 20, 2019.

The LICI was absolutely justified in applying before the Registrar, Original Side for return of the sums deposited and the Registrar, Original Side cannot be faulted for seeking clarification from this Court.

Even today, in the application filed by the appellants,
being IA No.GA/8/2023, there is not a shred of evidence or order produced to restrain the LICI from claiming sums of money as it was entitled to in terms of the order dated December 20, 2019 (supra).
(c) In the case of Dy. Director, Land Acquisition -vs- Malla Atchinaidu & ors.

entities.text: Dy. Director, Land Acquisition -vs- Malla Atchinaidu & ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(supra), the Supreme Court, at paragraph 8, had particularly observed that once a court passes an order, it cannot subsequently set aside or alter the same, however,
wrong it may appear to be.
It can only be done in an appeal, as observed by the Supreme Court.
The said case was in the context of compensation under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

(d) The facts and circumstsances of the said case are completely different from the facts of the instant case where certain contingencies were contemplated by a co-ordinate Bench in the order dated December 20, 2019 (supra).
11.
After the order was dictated, Mr. Sen submits that there were talks of settlement between the LICI and the appellants and adjournments were being taken before the revisional court.

The conduct of the LICI, in the same breath, to seek return of sums deposited, according to Mr. Sen,
would amount to a sharp practice.
12. This Court is of the view that the issues before a revisional court cannot be gone into by a Division Bench of this Court.
The question of recall of the order dated July 11, 2023 does not and cannot arise.
13. The order dated 20th December 2019 has left remedies open to the parties.

14. This Court is of the view that the application being IA No.GA/8/2023 is an abuse of the process of law and hence the same is dismissed with costs assessed at Rs.17000/-, payable by the applicants to the LICI.
